clue.text: Nationalist Irishman's in charge after civil unrest

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming after means being placed to the right of what precedes it

parts.note: Pat is a stock Irish first name, short for Patrick
a riot is a disturbance by a crowd

explanation.surface: An Irish nationalist takes control in the aftermath of street disturbances.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriotic person is devoted to their country, which is what a nationalist claims to be.

clue.text: Brought in by tube, Johnny's back about one

indicators.note: going back means the surname is read from its end towards its start
about means going round, so the reversed name wraps around the next piece

explanation.surface: Something delivered through a pipe, plus a Johnny turned round.
explanation.walkthrough: Johnny needs a famous surname: Depp, reversed to PPED, then wrapped round I to make PIPED.
explanation.definitionFit: Water or gas that is piped has been carried in through a conduit or pipe.

clue.text: Argentine cultivated fruit

indicators.note: cultivated land is worked over, so the letters are turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: A fruit grown commercially in Argentina.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small citrus fruit, a kind of mandarin orange.

clue.text: With road up, meeting could be out of the question

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the road's name is read bottom to top

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, with the digit 1 read as the letter I
if a meeting could happen, it is possible

explanation.surface: Roadworks mean a planned meeting may have to be called off.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a British motorway; the digit 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impossible cannot happen, so it is ruled out entirely.

clue.text: Prepare Queen to come in to land

indicators.note: the royal abbreviation is told to come inside the other word

parts.note: to train is to prepare for something

explanation.surface: Getting ready for the monarch's plane to touch down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to land' looks like an instruction to the plane; land is the definition, as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is a stretch of ground considered for its physical features.

clue.text: Company's top man meant heartless remark

indicators.note: without a heart, the word loses its central letter
the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written before its middle letter goes

explanation.surface: A firm's boss made an unkind observation.
explanation.walkthrough: MEANT has five letters, so heartless removes its middle A to leave MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A comment is a spoken or written observation, the same as a remark.

clue.text: Have no medicine that contains poison

indicators.note: the preceding words hold the target inside them, running across the word breaks

parts.note: the letters sit across the three words

explanation.surface: Someone refuses a remedy because it has toxic ingredients.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom is the poison injected by snakes, spiders and similar creatures.

clue.text: Quarrel over housing for climbing animal

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading from the bottom upwards
the two words house the target inside them, across the gap

parts.note: the last two letters of one word and first two of the next

explanation.surface: A dispute about building homes for a creature that climbs trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing animal' looks like the definition, but climbing is the reversal signal and only animal defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A vole is a small rodent related to the mouse, so it is an animal.

clue.text: Push on out of crumbling dungeon

indicators.note: something crumbling falls apart, so its letters are rebuilt in another order
taking one thing out of another means removing those letters

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: A prisoner shoves on to escape a collapsing cell.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove ON from DUNGEON to leave DUNGE, then rearrange those five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To nudge is to give a gentle push, often with the elbow.

clue.text: Island that developed a new cocktail?

definitions.text: Island that developed a new cocktail?

parts.words: Island that developed a new cocktail?
parts.note: surface reading: some island where a fresh mixed drink was invented

parts.words: Island that developed a new cocktail?
parts.note: setter's reading: the New York island borough that also names a whiskey and vermouth cocktail

explanation.walkthrough: The cocktail is named after the island on which New York City's centre sits, so one word answers both halves.
explanation.definitionFit: The island borough of New York shares its name with the classic whiskey cocktail invented there.

clue.text: Baby seal's over popular as poster subject

indicators.note: one piece lies over the other, covering it on both sides

parts.note: a young seal is a pup

explanation.surface: A cute seal pup is so popular its picture goes on bedroom walls.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin-up is a person, often a celebrity, whose photo is pinned up on a wall.

clue.text: Talked incessantly to academic on walk

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another follows it

parts.note: a ramble is a leisurely walk
a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: Someone chatters non-stop to a professor while out hiking.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To ramble on is an idiom for talking at length without getting to the point.

clue.text: Producer's chasing costume for seamstress

indicators.note: something chasing comes behind, so this piece goes after the other

parts.note: dress is clothing, as in fancy dress

explanation.surface: A film producer hunts for a costume for a seamstress character.
explanation.definitionFit: A seamstress sews clothes for a living, which is the job of a dressmaker.

clue.text: New game's wicked

indicators.note: a new version of the word has its letters freshly arranged

explanation.surface: A gamer's verdict that a new release is great.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' is slang praise here, not a word for evil.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal slang words of approval meaning excellent or great.

clue.text: Town's supporting return of its beer in spring

indicators.note: in a down clue, a supporting piece sits underneath, so it comes last
returning means going back, so the words that follow are read in reverse

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: A town backs the comeback of its local brew in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' suggests the season, but here it means bounce.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring in a material is its springiness or resilience, which is elasticity.

clue.text: Nothing to prevent a bird from flying, in theory

parts.note: zero, nothing, looks like the letter O

parts.words: to prevent a bird from flying
parts.note: to pinion a bird is to clip or bind its wing

explanation.surface: Arguing that, theoretically, nothing could keep a bird grounded.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a view held without proof, much like a personal theory.

clue.text: Sacked when blooming oaf botched task

parts.note: flowers that are blooming are out

indicators.note: a botched thing is badly put together, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A clumsy worker is fired after messing up the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blooming' looks like a mild British curse on the oaf, but it means in flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sacked has been dismissed from work, leaving them unemployed.

clue.text: Highest of everybody in exam

indicators.note: one word is placed inside the other

explanation.surface: Someone scored top marks of the whole class in a test.
explanation.definitionFit: The tallest thing reaches higher than any other, so it is the highest.

clue.text: Dear old love's thoughtful

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: A letter beginning 'Dear', about a former partner in a reflective mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear' looks like a term of affection, but it means costly.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear in the sense of high-priced means the same as costly.

clue.text: Novel, The Slap, has many ups and downs

definitions.note: noun phrase; 'has' links it to the wordplay

indicators.note: a novel version is a new one, so the letters are made into something fresh

explanation.surface: A book review: the novel The Slap is full of highs and lows.
explanation.walkthrough: The Slap is a real novel by Christos Tsiolkas, which makes 'Novel' read as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The European mountain range is a landscape of peaks and valleys, literally up and down.

clue.text: Help in seedy taverns

indicators.note: something seedy is run-down and disreputable, so the letters are knocked about

explanation.surface: Staff wanted at some run-down pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Help' is a noun here, as in domestic help.
explanation.definitionFit: Household help is an old term for domestic staff, such as a maid or butler.

clue.text: Goes with brush to clean toilet

definitions.note: a verb phrase describing the noun answer

parts.note: to dust is to clean surfaces
the pan is the toilet bowl

explanation.surface: Someone takes a scrubbing brush to clean the lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: A dustpan is the scoop paired with a small hand brush for sweeping up.

clue.text: Put off action capture amateur

indicators.note: to capture something is to hold it inside

explanation.surface: Postponing a move to arrest an untrained person.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something off is to postpone it, so it is delayed.

clue.text: Record change of life

indicators.note: a change makes the word different by rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: Keeping a note of a midlife transition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of life' is an idiom for the menopause, steering the reader away from wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A file is a collection of documents kept as a record.

clue.text: Purple patch regularly follows ill wind

indicators.note: the selected letters come after the twisted piece
to wind is to twist, so the letters are turned into a new order
taking letters at regular intervals means every other one

explanation.surface: A bad stretch, with stomach trouble, comes after a sickness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill wind' reads as an idiom, but wind is the verb meaning twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a pale purple colour named after the shrub's flowers.

clue.text: One brain cell mutation results in genius

indicators.note: a mutation alters the make-up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A single mutated neuron turns someone into a genius.
explanation.definitionFit: Genius as a quality means exceptional intellect, the same as brilliance.

clue.text: Very willing listener welcomes good ending to tale

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in
the ending of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A keen listener is delighted when a story ends happily.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager means keen and impatient to do something.

clue.text: Sing praises of that man on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio things are heard, not seen, so only the sound counts

explanation.surface: A broadcaster praising a man on air.
explanation.walkthrough: HYMN is used here as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To hymn someone is to praise or celebrate them, as in a song of worship.

clue.text: Jack's belly is upset by a rotten sweet

parts.note: J is the jack in a pack of cards

indicators.note: an upset stomach is churned, so the letters are rearranged
rotten things fall apart, so these letters are also shuffled

explanation.surface: Jack has stomach ache from eating a bad sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams; 'rotten sweet' reads as one phrase but rotten works on the words before it. Jelly babies are British baby-shaped gummy sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: A jelly baby is a soft gummy confection, a kind of sweet or candy.

clue.text: Setter's heard to inform on cake decoration

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I

indicators.note: heard means we go by the sound when spoken

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing to the police

explanation.surface: A crossword setter confesses about decorating a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inform on' is the phrase for snitching; 'on' then links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing is the sugary coating spread on cakes to decorate them.

clue.text: Rasher coming over without taxi?

definitions.note: a rasher is a single slice of the answer

indicators.note: turned over means the word is flipped end to end

parts.note: something coming on stage, or on its way, is on

explanation.surface: A reckless person walks over rather than taking a taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose clue: 'Rasher' poses as 'more rash', and 'without taxi' suggests arriving on foot, but the words work separately. A rasher is a slice of bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasher is a thin strip of bacon, so the clue defines by example.

clue.text: Criminal betrayed when 500 found inside cuddly toy

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other
something criminal is bent, so the letters are twisted out of order

explanation.surface: A crook is betrayed when a stash of money turns up inside a stuffed toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A teddy bear is the classic soft toy children cuddle.
